notes:
I couldn't do the research, so I have no notes on Psalm 50 to give you.

My first attempt to fetch sources returned an error saying I had no tool calls left for this turn, so no pages loaded. Your rules say to report only what the pages actually say and never to fill gaps from my own knowledge, so I haven't written any commentary from memory.

If you send the request again, these are the pages I planned to read first:

- **Verse-by-verse traditional readings:**
  - Enduring Word (David Guzik): enduringword.com/bible-commentary/psalm-50/
  - Gill on Biblehub: biblehub.com/commentaries/gill/psalms/50.htm
  - Ellicott on Biblehub: biblehub.com/commentaries/ellicott/psalms/50.htm
  - Pulpit Commentary and Biblehub's per-verse pages
  - Precept Austin and StudyLight
- **Protestant traditions:**
  - Spurgeon's *Treasury of David* (Baptist), on spurgeon.org or StudyLight
  - Wesley's *Explanatory Notes* (Methodist), on wesley.nnu.edu
  - Ligonier and The Gospel Coalition (Reformed)
  - LCMS and 1517 (Lutheran)
  - Desiring God and GTY (Baptist)
- **Other views:**
  - NET Bible notes for modern scholarship, especially on vv. 5, 14 and 23
  - Augustine's exposition on New Advent. Older Catholic numbering follows the Greek Psalter, so this psalm is listed there as Psalm 49: newadvent.org/fathers/1801049.htm
  - Catholic.com and OCA
  - For the "cattle on a thousand hills" verse (v. 10) and prosperity teaching, I'd search Got Questions, Desiring God and GTY, since it's often cited in that debate.
